title: Maritime Space Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
4.     MOS 1706, Maritime Space Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Maritime Space Officers (MSO) serve as the principal
advisor for integration of space effects and capabilities into fleet marine
force (FMF) operations. They serve as commanders and staff officers in the
FMF, on joint assignments, and in key billets throughout the information
community. MSOs are responsible for the deliberate, detailed planning and
employment of space capabilities and effects, as well as the coordination and
integration of space operations into a unit’s overall scheme of maneuver.
They evaluate both friendly and adversary capabilities, and develop,
coordinate, and execute approved space operations activities.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement:         must have a current T5 investigation and
adjudicated for SCI eligibility.

            (3) Lateral move additional prerequisites:

                (a) Must have accepted career designation.

            (b) Must be worldwide deployable at the time SNO is approved for
lateral move into the 1706 MOS.

            (c) All applicants must be screened and recommended for a lateral
move by a screening panel in accordance with the applicable lateral move
solicitation MARADMIN message.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Space Operations Officer Qualification Course
(SOOQC), (F25M5K4), US Army Space and Missile Defense Center of Excellence
(USA SMDCoE), Colorado Springs, CO.

        (2) Complete the MAGTF Operations in the Information Environment
Practitioner Course (MOPC) (M02F2GD), Quantico, VA.

        (3) SNO is granted the 1706 MOS upon graduation from SOOQC and MOPC.
MOS training validation and MOS granting authority is managed by the
Information Maneuver OccFld manager, DC I.




                                            1-85                        Enclosure (1)
 1114                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



        (4) Any of these requirements may be waived by the deputy commandant
for Information based on unique work or educational experience.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Influence Officer, 1707.

            (2) Space Operations Staff Officer, 1786.

            (3) Special Technical Operations Planner, 8016.

            (4) Space Operations Officer, 8866.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
